title: xmltodict: unparse() writes the text 'None' for None values
prompt: `xmltodict.unparse` writes the literal text "None" when a None value is inside an element dict: >>> from xmltodict import unparse >>> unparse({"a": {"@param": "test", "#text": None}}, full_document=False) 'None' # wrong, should be '' None must be written as an empty value, for text and for attributes: - `unparse({"a": {"@param": "test", "#text": None}}, full_document=False) == ''` - `unparse({"x": {"@pro": None}}, full_document=False) == ''` - `unparse({"x": {"#text": None, "@pro": None}, "y": None}, short_empty_elements=True, full_document=False) == ''` - `unparse({"a": None}, full_document=False)` equals `unparse({"a": {"#text": None}}, full_document=False)`. Other non-string text (True, numbers) keeps its current output. One existing test in tests/test_dicttoxml.py (test_non_string_text_with_attributes) asserts the old, wrong output for a None #text. It will be replaced by a corrected version, so update that line as needed. The code is in xmltodict.py. Run the existing tests with: python -m pytest -q tests/test_dicttoxml.py
